description: Harappa and Mohenjo-daro — planned brick cities with drainage, seals, and long-distance trade — mark South Asia's first urban age.

eventTitle: Later Vedic world on the Ganga plain
description: Pastoral and agrarian janapadas take shape; ritual and philosophical texts of the later Vedic corpus are composed.
Northern India organises into large kingdoms and oligarchies; Magadha begins its rise from the eastern Gangetic plain.
Siddhartha Gautama attains awakening at Bodh Gaya. The Bodhi tree precinct remains a living pilgrimage centre.
With Chanakya, Chandragupta Maurya overturns the Nandas and builds the first pan-Indian imperial state, later described in the Arthashastra tradition.
The Kalinga campaign's slaughter turns Ashoka toward dhamma. His edicts, carved from Kandahar to Karnataka, are among India's earliest dated public texts.
Mauryan brick core, Shunga and Satavahana gateways: Sanchi becomes a textbook of early Buddhist art.
Under Kanishka and successors, Silk Road Kushan power funds monasteries; Buddha is widely shown in human form in Gandhara and Mathura.
From Magadha, the Guptas preside over a flowering of Sanskrit literature, mathematics, and temple beginnings often called India's classical golden age.
Vakataka-period viharas and chaityas in a Waghora gorge receive their famous murals of Jataka stories and courtly life.
Rashtrakuta patrons have a whole Shiva mountain carved downward from the Deccan basalt — among the world's largest monolithic excavations.
Rajaraja I completes the great Chola vimana at Thanjavur, a granite statement of imperial Shaivism.
Ghaznavid campaigns into the north, including Somnath, mark a new era of contact — and conflict — between Central Asian armies and Indian kingdoms.
Qutb-ud-din Aibak's line begins more than three centuries of sultanate rule from Delhi, leaving the Qutb complex and a Persianate court culture.
A cluster of Nagara temples, including Kandariya Mahadeva, is raised in Bundelkhand with some of India's most celebrated sculpture.
Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty commissions a colossal stone chariot for Surya on the Odisha coast.
Harihara and Bukka establish a Hindu imperial capital on the Tungabhadra. Hampi's ruins still map its sacred and royal core.
Deccan sultanates defeat Vijayanagara; Hampi is sacked, and the empire's political centre shifts south.
Babur defeats Ibrahim Lodi and founds Mughal rule in northern India.
Jalal-ud-din Muhammad Akbar expands Mughal power, experiments with sulh-i-kul, and builds Fatehpur Sikri as a short-lived capital.
Shah Jahan begins the marble mausoleum for Mumtaz Mahal on the Yamuna at Agra, finished in the 1640s with a charbagh and mosque-jawab pair.
The court moves to a new walled city in Delhi; the Lal Qila becomes the ceremonial heart of later Mughal emperors.
At Raigad, Shivaji Bhonsle is crowned, giving the Maratha polity a sovereign centre that will later challenge Mughal supremacy.
Birth of Guru Nanak in the Punjab. Sikh teaching of ik onkar, langar, and rejection of caste privilege takes root; Harmandir Sahib later becomes its architectural focus.
Clive's victory over Siraj-ud-Daulah, aided by treachery within Bengal, opens Company dominion in eastern India.
A widespread uprising against the East India Company — Meerut, Delhi, Kanpur, Lucknow, Jhansi — ends Company rule and brings the Crown.
Aibak starts the victory minaret beside the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque; Iltutmish and later sultans raise it to its present height.

eventTitle: Madurai Nayak rebuilding of Meenakshi temple
description: Under Tirumala Nayaka the vast temple-city of Meenakshi-Sundareshwarar takes much of its present processional form.
Guru Arjan installs the Adi Granth in the newly built Harmandir Sahib, the tank-girt centre of Sikh worship.
Troops under General Dyer fire on an unarmed gathering in Amritsar. The massacre radicalises the national movement.
Gandhi's first nationwide satyagraha campaign after Jallianwala and the Khilafat moment draws millions into organised boycott.
Gandhi walks from Sabarmati to the sea to make salt, turning a tax into a global symbol of civil disobedience.
With World War II underway, Congress demands immediate British withdrawal; a fierce underground and street struggle follows mass arrests.
On 15 August India becomes independent. Partition of British India creates Pakistan and triggers vast, violent displacement.
The Constitution drafted under Ambedkar's chairmanship comes into force on 26 January; India becomes a sovereign democratic republic.
Indian forces end 451 years of Portuguese rule in Goa, Daman, and Diu.
High-yield wheat, irrigation, and credit transform north-western agriculture and make India broadly self-sufficient in grain.
A balance-of-payments crisis opens a programme of reform that recasts industry, trade, and later India's services economy.
UNESCO lists the Vijayanagara ruins at Hampi, recognising the boulder landscape of temples, bazaars, and royal enclosures.
The mausoleum complex is inscribed as a World Heritage Site, later drawing tens of millions of visitors a decade.
